title: Dog-Trade Defenses Need Proof, Quarantine, and Abolition
excerpt: Claims about tradition and farm-raised dogs cannot erase missing traceability, quarantine, or protection for family animals. Vietnam needs transparent reform and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
When a family dog disappears, grief begins before any trade claim can be tested. Yet no specific seizure, conviction, location, date, or official dataset is documented here to prove that every animal entering Vietnam’s dog-meat trade was stolen. That gap does not protect the trade. It exposes a system demanding public trust without transparent traceability.

Tradition cannot replace proof

“Farm-raised” is a claim, not a supply-chain record. A credible system would document origin, ownership, transport permits, veterinary inspection, quarantine compliance, and slaughter conditions. Without those records, no reader can honestly treat every animal as legally sourced. Lawful activity, regulatory breaches, and criminal pet theft require separate proof. None should hide behind tradition.

Biosecurity starts before exposure

Rabies is transmitted when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Handling sick animals, bite attacks, and uninspected slaughter can create risk; properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance supports immediate care.

Transparency before permission

Household rabies exposure and commercial supply-chain failures are parallel biosecurity problems, not proof of one causing the other. Public authorities need enforceable quarantine, transport inspection, ownership records, and action against proven theft networks. Vietnamese families and local leaders can demand those protections without shaming communities or confusing lawful conduct with crime.

SDE’s demand goes further than any single health target: complete national abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for traceability now and abolition by 2030.
